name: MailcatcherClient
author: Johannes Przymusinski

sections.description:
Mailcatcher for WordPress seamlessly connects your WordPress site to Mailcatcher, a cloud-based service designed to capture and display emails sent from development and test environments. This integration ensures that no real emails are dispatched during testing, allowing developers to review and debug email content safely and efficiently.

Key features include:

  • Effortless Integration: Redirect all outgoing emails from your WordPress site to Mailcatcher without complex configurations.
  • Multi-Project Support: Organize test emails by project within Mailcatcher, maintaining clarity across multiple development initiatives.
  • User Permissions & Sharing: Collaborate with team members or clients by granting tailored access to specific projects and their associated emails.
  • Cloud-Based Convenience: Access your intercepted emails anytime, anywhere, without the need for local installations or server setups.
  • Seamless Attachment Handling: View, download, and test email attachments directly within the Mailcatcher interface.

For more information about Mailcatcher and its features, visit https://mailcatcher.dev/.
sections.installation:
1. Install the Plugin:

    • Download the plugin ZIP file.
    • Navigate to the ‘Plugins’ section in your WordPress dashboard.
    • Click ‘Add New’ and then ‘Upload Plugin’.
    • Upload the ZIP file and activate the plugin.

  2. Configure Mailcatcher Settings:

    • After activation, go to ‘Settings’ > ‘Mailcatcher’ in your WordPress dashboard.
    • Enter your Mailcatcher credentials, including the tenant and project slugs, as well as the project password. These credentials can be found in your Mailcatcher project settings.
    • Save your changes.

  3. Test Email Interception:

    • Use the “Send Test Email” action in the plugin settings.
    • or perform any action on your WordPress site that triggers an email (e.g., password reset, new user registration).
    • Log in to your Mailcatcher account and navigate to the corresponding project to view the intercepted email.
sections.faq:
What is Mailcatcher?

Mailcatcher is a cloud-based service that captures emails sent from development and test environments, allowing developers to view and debug them in a user-friendly web interface. It helps ensure that no real emails are sent during testing, preventing unintended communications.

Is Mailcatcher for WordPress compatible with other email plugins?

Mailcatcher for WordPress is designed to work independently by redirecting all outgoing emails to the Mailcatcher service. While it should function alongside other email plugins, conflicts may arise if multiple plugins attempt to override the default email sending behavior. It’s recommended to test compatibility in your development environment.

Can I use Mailcatcher for WordPress on a live site?

This plugin is intended for use in development and testing environments. Using it on a live site would redirect all outgoing emails to Mailcatcher, preventing real emails from reaching their intended recipients. It’s not recommended for production use.

How do I manage multiple projects with Mailcatcher?

Mailcatcher supports multi-project management, allowing you to organize test emails by project. Within your Mailcatcher account, you can create separate projects for different development initiatives and configure your WordPress sites to send emails to the corresponding project’s SMTP credentials.

Is there a cost associated with using Mailcatcher?

Mailcatcher offers various pricing plans, including a free tier with basic functionality. For detailed information on available plans and features, visit Mailcatcher Pricing.
